transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
International climate change negotiations in Turkey broke down in the final hours on
Sunday.
NPR's Lauren Summer reports.
The key sticking point was over fossil fuels.
Countries were negotiating an agreement to move away from using energy like coal and
natural gas, which produced heat-trapping emissions that warmed the planet.
Countries like Saudi Arabia rejected that language, leading the European Union and others
to walk out.
The U.S. was not at the negotiations.
Fossil fuels were part of a climate deal agreed to back in 2023.
Now, some countries are questioning the value of the United Nations climate talks.
Most countries are not on track to meet their pledges to cut emissions.
Lauren Summer, NPR News.
If you were flying today, there's a good chance on Delta Airlines you were delayed.
The airline reported problems with an automated system used to calculate the weight and balance
of its planes, NPR's Andrea Shue reports.
For a good part of the day, Delta Airlines said it used manual workarounds to safely
get flights off the ground.
By mid-afternoon, the automation was once again working.
The airline says it's re-booking passengers and providing meals and hotel rooms where necessary.
The problems come just over a week after the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide
ground stop that halted take-offs for more than four hours.
Officials said some maintenance work on an aging system was to blame.
With Thanksgiving approaching, AAA projects some six million people will be flying this
week.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
Palestinian officials say Israeli settlers were behind a series of arson attacks early
Sunday that caused hundreds of thousands of dollars of property damage in the Israeli-occupied
West Bank.
NPR's Noha Mosele reports from Ramallah.
Palestinian farmer Abdel Fattah Hamayil says he woke up to Israeli settlers setting fire
to cars outside his home north of Ramallah.
He says the Israeli army arrived and took photos of the damage, including graffiti that
said death to Arabs and Hebrew, but offered no help to residents.
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Isinkot called the arson attacks Jewish terrorism and blamed
far-right ministers in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet for stoking violence.
Isinkot is leading coalition talks to try to oust Netanyahu and succeed him as prime
minister.
For NPR News, I'm Noha Mosele and Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
It will be a short week on Wall Street because of the Thanksgiving holiday markets to be
closed Thursday and only open until 1 p.m. Eastern on Friday.
Two major companies in the tech sector, Dell Technologies and Hewlett Packer will announce
earnings after tech stocks had a big drop on Friday.
From Washington, this is NPR.
The death of a beloved hippo, Fiona, after she swallowed a knit hat has renewed calls
to remind zoo visitors that animals can die from swallowing foreign objects.
NPR's Shonda Lee Stuster reports.
While deaths like Fiona the hippos are rare, items such as coins, shoes and sunglasses
frequently fall and sometimes are tossed into animal habitats at zoos.
Dr. Gabriela Flaca, a veterinarian at Zoo Miami, asked that visitors follow zoo etiquette
and not yell or throw objects at the animals.
If we can just keep in mind that anything that we bring that could inadvertently end
up in the animal exhibit or somehow around the animal, try to just be mindful and not
have your sunglasses on your head if you're leaning over and looking at something.
Veterinarians say people should also be mindful of items that can harm animals in the wild
or even pets at home.
Human medication should be stored properly and trash should be thrown into a garbage can
so animals cannot eat it.
Shonda Lee Stuster, NPR News.
Democrats have picked up another seat in the House of Representatives, this time in North
Carolina where Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated 11-term Republican Congresswoman Virginia
Foxx by 331 votes.
A recount was completed Sunday and Foxx conceded.
In North Carolina, Democrats will send 11 members to Washington Republicans 3.
It is a reversal of the 10-to-4 majority Republicans had in the last Congress.
Democrats will now have at least 258 votes in the House of Representatives.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News.

topics.text: International climate talks in Turkey collapse over fossil fuel language; European Union walks out
Delta Airlines suffers automated weight-and-balance system failure, delaying flights nationwide
Palestinian officials say Israeli settlers set arson fires damaging property in West Bank
Wall Street to close Thursday and close early Friday for Thanksgiving; Dell and HP report earnings
Death of hippo Fiona after swallowing knit hat prompts reminders about zoo visitor behavior
Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeats Republican Virginia Foxx in North Carolina House race by 331 votes
